findings.text: Outer user transition helpers first abandon work when current execution is inside interrupt handling, otherwise they preserve interrupt masking across delegation to inner helpers that assume interrupts are already masked. One helper covers entry toward user or guest execution and the other covers return toward kernel execution, each accepting a context kind parameter.

Inner enter and exit helpers operate on the current CPU tracking record and apply a recursion guard so nested invocations leave immediately. They act only when the recorded context differs from or matches the requested context respectively, and they distinguish CPUs with tracking active from CPUs where only bookkeeping is maintained for migration consistency.

A per CPU nesting counter permits only the outermost tracking transition to proceed. The first increment reports permission while deeper nesting triggers a one time diagnostic on invalid values, reverses the increment, and reports denial; a paired decrement releases permission after the outermost work completes.
Two small callable wrappers provide stable entry symbols that forward to the generic user enter and user exit operations without additional logic.

Early initialization marks every possible CPU as tracked and raises a global static branch once per CPU, with the first activation also propagating a no tick thread flag to the initial task and diagnosing unexpected additional tasks. A separate iterator applies this activation across all possible CPUs.

Each CPU owns a hotplug progression record holding current, desired, and failure injection positions plus thread wake coordination, rollback and single step markers, bringup direction, instance iteration resume position, callback outcome, atomic synchronization word, and paired completions for upward and downward movement. The initial failure marker denotes invalid.

A hotplug step descriptor carries a human readable name, separate startup and teardown callback groups each supporting one shot and per instance forms, a list head linking registered instances, and flags indicating whether stopping is forbidden and whether multiple instances exist. Helpers resolve a descriptor from its state value and test whether the callback needed for a given direction is missing.

Callback invocation first honors an injected failure for the requested position, then treats a missing directional callback as a diagnostic success. One shot steps invoke a single callback while multi instance steps either invoke one supplied instance or walk all registered instances until completion or error, recording progress for resumable walks and reversing already completed instances through the opposite directional callbacks when a non resumable walk fails.

Target programming captures the prior position, clears rollback and resume markers, records the new target and direction derived from ordering, resets single stepping, and aligns the dying indication with direction. Rollback preparation points back at the prior target, marks rollback, adjusts the current position unless a partial multi instance walk must be undone first, reverses direction, and realigns the dying indication.

Application and control CPUs coordinate through a per CPU atomic word that moves among dead, kicked, dying request, alive, online request, and online conditions. The control side uses a bounded wait that polls briefly before sleeping and reports failure on timeout, while the application side publishes its condition and spins until released. Builds without full synchronization replace these operations with no operation variants.
A dedicated mutex serializes CPU map updates and hotplug disable accounting, with paired begin and done helpers that acquire and release it around counter changes.

CPU presence protection uses a percpu read write semaphore with try lock read access, exclusive write access, and held state queries for diagnostics. Separate directional lockdep maps distinguish upward and downward traversals, with acquire and release shims that become empty when diagnostic tracking is disabled, alongside explicit lockdep acquire and release helpers for the presence lock.
A global mutex guards the table of hotplug step descriptors against concurrent registration and lookup.

Atomicity is decided by membership in a bounded interval ending before online completion, while application CPU responsibility is decided by exceeding the bringup threshold with an explicit exclusion for the teardown position.

Kicking an application thread skips already satisfied targets unless single stepping, otherwise clears the outcome, orders prior stores before publishing the run request, wakes the thread, and waits on the directional completion. A failing kick triggers rollback preparation followed by a second kick. The online wait additionally unparks the target thread and can veto completion when the CPU is not bootable.

Threading control combines a global mode, a maximum thread count fixed after boot, and a current thread limit defaulting to the largest value. Forced or ordinary disable paths record the mode, announce the change, and collapse the limit to one. Thread count configuration validates inputs, marks unsupported hardware when appropriate, and reconciles requested counts with the current mode. Boot eligibility favors enabled threading, unconfigured controls, unsupported hardware, primary threads, and CPUs never booted before.

Diagnostics and failure handling include one time warnings for invalid nesting, kernel threads entering user mode, missing directional callbacks, failed rollbacks, and unexpected online state, plus error logs and failure codes when an application CPU does not report dead or alive conditions in time or when hotplug enable is unbalanced.
Hotplug suppression uses counters guarded by the map mutex: one flag permanently disables offlining while another counts nested disable requests with balanced enable that diagnoses underflow.

Architecture integration points provide default empty definitions for synchronization polling, dead CPU cleanup, kicked CPU cleanup, and threading updates, alongside explicit report dead and report alive entry points and a tracepoint creation marker for this translation unit.
A global boolean records whether tasks are frozen for hotplug coordination, co located with the map mutex definition.

Boot attempt preparation inspects the atomic synchronization word and permits only properly dead, previously kicked, or alive but waiting conditions, transitioning accepted cases toward kicked through compare exchange with retry, and vetoing any other limbo condition. A configuration without full synchronization always permits boot.
